hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the suite, plus my own attacks on the product as built
hard_gates.evidence: Over HTTP, signed in as alnoor (A), I attacked gulfsteel (B) (attack-http.txt). I sent PUT /api/identity/me/preferences with B's userId, tenantId and id in the body and query, and with the X-Tenant-Id, X-Tenant, X-Workspace and X-User-Id headers. Each call changed only A's own row. GET /identity/users/{B id} returned 404. Searching users for 'gulfsteel' returned 0 rows. GET /auth/session with B's tenant header still answered as A. B's preferences were unchanged afterwards. As the database role erp_app (attack-db-app-role.txt): an unbound read of identity.users and audit.entries returned 0 rows, UPDATE of B's user affected 0 rows, and SET row_security=off was refused. erp_app, erp_owner and erp_auth have no BYPASSRLS. In the real product on a shared tab, A's palette showed only A's records after B signed out (shared-device-product.txt). In the suite under machine load, the G1 HTTP test passed. In my P5 run it ran 51 endpoints with 41,699 requests and 46 write pairs.

hard_gates.gate: G1 catches a tenant leak planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: P5 (caught). In PUT /me/preferences I held the last caller's e-mail in AppContext.SetData, a BCL store that no product static inventories, and appended it to displayName. G1HttpIsolationTests failed with 8 leaks, from the write-after-write and B-reads-before phases. The round-1 gap is fixed. P9 (missed). This piece's command palette (web/src/modules/shell/CommandPalette.tsx) got a module-level Map that caches record-source answers by query. Nothing clears it at sign-out. The web type-check, string and accessibility checks passed, and so did the unit tests (93/93). The end-to-end suite against the planted build passed 34/34 on its second run; on the first, 33 passed and 1 failed in an unrelated preferences-save test, which the control and the rerun did not reproduce. The .NET gates cannot see client state. Live demo on the planted build (plants/P9/live-demo.txt, 11-planted-P9-palette-after-switch.jpg): admin@gulfsteel.example searches 'admin' in the palette and signs out, then admin@alnoor.example signs in on the same tab. Typing 'admin' then shows A gulfsteel's users admin@gulfsteel.example and admin.ar@gulfsteel.example. No end-to-end spec signs in as two tenants in one browser.

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: every action is denied unless a role grants it
hard_gates.evidence: P6b: I added .AllowAnonymous() after RequirePermission(ProfileUpdate) on PUT /me/preferences. Three G2PermissionTests failed (no-grant user, exactly-one-permission, and anonymous gets 401). The static test Every_endpoint_declares_exactly_one_permission_or_is_reviewed_anonymous passed and did not notice. P8: I removed the shell's route permission guard in AppShell.tsx. SignInPage.test.tsx 'refuses an address the roles do not allow' failed. P7: I removed the client-side can(identity.profile.update) check before saving preferences. 93/93 unit tests passed, but the server still refuses (403 leads to 'refused'), so no action is opened. That is a test gap, not a hole.

biggest_gap.title: The shell's client state is outside every isolation gate: a palette cache that survives sign-out shows tenant B's users to tenant A, and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail: The G1 machinery covers only the server: routes, database, process state and headers. The shell is a single-page app that stays in memory across sign-out and the next sign-in, and no gate or test ever signs in as two tenants in one browser. So any module-level cache, store or memoised answer in the shell or a palette source leaks the previous tenant's records to the next user of the same tab. A UAE trading company's outsourced bookkeeper, serving several client companies (tenants) from one browser, is exactly that user. The real product shows a milder form of the same thing today: after tenant B signs out, the sign-in page is pre-filled with B's e-mail (erp.lastEmail in localStorage, SignInPage.tsx:6-14). Fix: (1) Make sign-out and every tenant change reload the document (location.assign) and clear the erp.* keys that belong to the user, so JS memory cannot carry over. (2) Add an end-to-end gate: in one tab, tenant B uses every palette source, list, screen and dialog with marker data, then signs out; tenant A signs in in the same tab, repeats the same actions, and the DOM, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB are judged for B's markers. (3) Keep plant P9 as the gate's self-test.
biggest_gap.evidence: Plant (plant-P9-palette-cache-survives-sign-out.diff): in CommandPalette.tsx, add `const answered = new Map<string, SourceState>()` at module level. Serve a hit for `${source.key}:${trimmed}` instead of asking the source, and store each answer. Results: tsc, the string and accessibility checks and the unit tests (93/93) passed. The end-to-end suite against the planted build passed 34/34 on its second run (plants/P9/e2e-2/e2e.log); the first run's one failure was an unrelated preferences-save flake. The .NET gates do not touch client code. Live (plants/P9/live-demo.txt): sign in as admin@gulfsteel.example, Ctrl+K, type 'admin', Esc, Sign out, then sign in as admin@alnoor.example in the same tab, Ctrl+K, type 'admin'. The palette lists 'admin@gulfsteel.example' and 'admin.ar@gulfsteel.example' (11-planted-P9-palette-after-switch.jpg). Unplanted product, same steps: A sees only alnoor users, but the sign-in page shows admin@gulfsteel.example pre-filled (shared-device-product.txt).

other_findings: BLOCKING [route: p05-list-search]: UsersListVolumeTests (tests/Erp.Modules.Identity.Tests/UsersListVolumeTests.cs:52-61, a 400 ms median budget and a 1000 ms ceiling for every single run, measured inside the full parallel suite) failed both clean-clone verify runs on this shared 4-CPU machine. Run 1: search median 604 ms and slowest 1130 ms; take=100 slowest 1076 ms. Run 2: filter slowest 1059 ms. Alone, the class passed 3/3. A per-run wall-clock ceiling inside a parallel suite on a shared machine fails G3. Options: run the volume class in a non-parallel collection, measure server time (for example EXPLAIN ANALYZE or a server timing header) instead of the round trip, or judge only the median.
